questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
questions.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 10\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 10\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=10.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & -5 \\ 3 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 3 & -2 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -10 \\ -10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
questions.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 6 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 3 & 3 & 21\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Given With Respect to the Standard Basis Under a Linear Map
questions.problem:
$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ (shown above) and a basis $C$ of ${R}^{3}.$
The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to these bases, and the vector $x\in {R}^{2},$ are also given. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
questions.worked_solution:
We can find the coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find $[x]_{B},$ the coordinates of $x$ relative to $B.$ So, let

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives us the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We now row-reduce the corresponding augmented matrix using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ -1 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+4{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 23 \\ 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}23 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}23 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -13 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Linear Map Relative to Two Bases Given One Basis
questions.problem:
Consider the basis $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ of the vector space $V$ and the basis $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ given by

$$
C={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T:V\to {R}^{2}$ relative to these bases if 

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}18 \\ 27\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $C.$

First, we need to find the coordinates of $T({b}_{i})$ relative to the basis $C$ for each $i=1,2,3.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the following matrix:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

We reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & 6 & 18 \\ 3 & -3 & -9 & -3 & 27\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 3 & -3 & -9 & -3 & 27\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & -12 & -9 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -7 & -4 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the right-hand side gives the matrix of the linear transformation relative to the bases $B$ and $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -4 & 12 \\ -4 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

questions.problem:
$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & -1 \\ 7 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Suppose $B$ and $C$ are bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W,$ respectively. The matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the linear map $T:V\to W$ relative to these bases, and the coordinates of the vector $x\in V$ relative to $B$ are shown above. Find $[T(x)]_{C}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The coordinates of the image of $x$ under $T$ relative to the basis $C$ can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[T(x)]_{C} & =[T]_{B|C}\cdot [x]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 & -1 \\ 7 & -2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}34 \\ 28\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
